ai_view.directive: Follow as written. Use two independent decisions: whether an operation is safe to continue, and whether provider contract drift has actually been established. Alert on observable risk, diagnose from independent evidence, and withdraw only the qualifications whose guarantees are no longer established. Repeated errors do not automatically prove contract drift; one decisive counterexample can.
ai_view.specification: Extend the in-build revocation-linearization spec (naya5/revocation-linearization) with AER-ALERT-1: the two-field incident model (operational response: OBSERVE/INVESTIGATE/HOLD_AFFECTED_RETRIES/BLOCK_AFFECTED_EXECUTION × evidence-based diagnosis: TRANSIENT_ANOMALY/SUSPECTED_DRIFT/CONTRACT_SCOPE_CHANGE/CONFIRMED_CONTRACT_BREACH/UNDETERMINED) preventing false accusation and false reassurance, with containment permitted before confirmed diagnosis but precaution explicitly distinguished from established fact in the historical record; the L0–L4 alert thresholds (L0 normal transient; L1 investigate with the illustrative statistical gate — ≥100 comparable requests, ≥5 anomalous, ≥3× baseline, prespecified statistical test, persistence or corroboration, calibrated per endpoint; L2 precautionary hold on credible possible duplicate for high-impact ops; L3 qualification withdrawn on ONE verified prohibited duplicate effect with no arbitrary minimum count; L4 wider incident with defensible exposure boundary) as proposed starting values, not ratified settings; the right denominators (timeout rate, rate-limit rate, ambiguous outcome rate per distinct logical operation, confirmed duplicate-effect rate over eligible observably-reconciled operations with unobserved outcomes disclosed, canary failures, observation coverage — one operation retried 20× is not 20 provider failures; always stratify by endpoint/version/tenant/region/effect/config/horizon); statistically calibrated thresholds for noisy signals (matched baselines, count models for low baselines, false-alert control across many endpoints, correlated-error handling, multi-window persistence — a confirmed duplicate bypasses statistical thresholds entirely); minimum evidence by diagnosis (his six-row table, with the 6-point checklist for a confirmed duplicate-effect counterexample: same logical operation, matching keys/payloads/scope, guarantee covered the scenario, two distinct prohibited material effects, authentic complete records, not duplicate webhooks/logs of one effect — provider-attributed breach additionally requires distinguishing provider behavior from client misuse); the HTTP symptom classifier (429/quota, 403-installation-token/quota vs 403-policy-refusal, 500/503, timeout, duplicate webhooks, two verified effects — with the NayaPOWER example: installation-token rate-limit 403 vs comment-lock-policy 403 share a status but need different actions, and the attribution still needs evidence checking before it counts as a verified causal finding); the two-stage alert engine (Stage A fast safety decision, Stage B slow independent diagnosis, Stage C requalification — his evaluate_provider_signal policy with the UNDETERMINED path and guarded atomic withdrawal); the T1–T10 false-positive/missed-drift suite (rate-limit bursts, lost acks, double webhooks, client key changes, one conclusive duplicate ⇒ immediate withdrawal, silent retention shortening, regional narrowing, single unclear canary failure, telemetry loss ⇒ observability gap not health, restoration ⇒ new qualification required — including near-misses that separate availability from correctness); the essential metrics (false drift attribution rate, unsafe continuation rate, detection latency, unnecessary qualification loss, evidence coverage, requalification validity — zero false definitive attributions and zero unsafe continued retries on sealed controls, with the finite-corpus honesty clause); atomic withdrawal at the LAW/ACT consequential-use boundary (new qualification version preserving the original + evidence, never history rewrite; KNOW/CONNECT/VERIFY/PROVE/LAW/ACT/LEARN each play their node role; resolved qualifications may narrow, never auto-restore provider-wide trust). The Provider Alert Evidence Law. Highest-value next test: AER-ALERT-001 (two controlled histories with identical timeout bursts — one healthy dedup, one silently duplicating; same initial transport assessment for both; divergent response once effect evidence arrives; repeat for rate-limit bursts, expired retention, downstream-only duplication — testing threshold → evidence → diagnosis → containment → requalification).

intelligence.essence: Provider Alert Evidence Law: NayaNET must not infer provider contract drift from ordinary transport errors, retry counts, or missing acknowledgments alone. Statistical thresholds may trigger investigation; independently verified contract changes or decisive effect violations establish qualification changes. Precautionary containment may occur earlier when necessary for safety, but must remain explicitly distinct from causal attribution. Unaffected operations and independently established guarantees remain available. The desired result is a system that can say: 'The provider is experiencing a rate-limit incident; idempotency drift is not established. This operation's outcome is still unknown, so I will reconcile it before retrying.' Or: 'Two prohibited material effects were independently verified for one qualified logical operation. The affected deduplication guarantee has been withdrawn, pending investigation and independent requalification.' Sensitive to real failures without becoming a machine that generates false alarms, unnecessary shutdowns, or unsupported accusations. The central law: alert on observable risk, diagnose from independent evidence, withdraw only what is no longer established — repeated errors don't prove drift; one decisive counterexample can.
intelligence.falsifier: Drift inferred from timeouts, retry counts, or missing acks alone; a single timeout declared a contract breach; a confirmed duplicate left retryable pending a trend; request-count denominators used for contract-correctness claims; unobserved outcomes silently excluded from the duplicate-effect denominator; incompatible scopes aggregated into one trend; HTTP status used as a root-cause classifier; precaution recorded as established fact; a restored error rate presented as requalification; one endpoint's recovery restoring provider-wide trust.

human_view.meaning: Two separate questions, never blurred: 'is it safe to keep going right now?' and 'has the provider actually broken its promise?' A burst of timeouts justifies investigating — not accusing. One proven double-charge justifies pulling the guarantee immediately — no waiting for a trend. The alert ladder runs from normal noise up through investigate, precautionary hold, withdrawal, and wider incident — with the statistics calibrated per endpoint and the honest note that these are starting values, not gospel. The denominators matter: count logical operations, not raw requests, and say out loud how many outcomes you couldn't observe. A confirmed duplicate needs a six-point proof — same operation, same keys, covered scenario, two genuinely distinct effects, authentic records, not just double webhooks. And the engine runs in two stages: a fast safety gate that can hold a dangerous retry now, and a slow careful diagnosis that names the cause later — with the record always distinguishing 'we held this to be safe' from 'we proved this broke.' The system we want can say both sentences: 'rate-limit incident, drift not established, reconciling before retry' and 'two prohibited effects verified, guarantee withdrawn pending requalification.' Sensitive to real failures, never a false-alarm machine.

intelligence.learning_lesson: This is the alerting discipline the drift monitor needed: AER-DRIFT-1 watches; AER-ALERT-1 decides and proves. The permanent contributions: the operational-severity × causal-diagnosis two-field model, the L0–L4 ladder with statistical calibration rules, the logical-operation denominators, the six-point duplicate-effect proof checklist, the HTTP-symptom classifier (status codes are inputs, not verdicts), the two-stage engine (fast safety, slow diagnosis), the T1–T10 suite with availability-vs-correctness near-misses, and the precaution-vs-fact record distinction. Every future monitoring system inherits this: alert on risk, diagnose on evidence, withdraw only what's disproven — and say which is which.

intelligence.measurement_contract: AER-ALERT-001: two controlled provider histories with identical initial timeout bursts (one healthy dedup, one silently duplicating); detector gives the same initial transport assessment to both; once independent effect evidence arrives, healthy provider investigated/resolved without false breach claim, defective provider's guarantee withdrawn; repeated for rate-limit bursts, expired retention, downstream-only duplication. T1–T10 suite: zero false definitive drift attributions on sealed negative controls, zero unsafe continued retries after authoritative withdrawal, all unaffected paths preserved. L1 statistical gates calibrated per endpoint with documented baselines, windows, and false-alert tolerance. Every L3 withdrawal backed by the six-point duplicate-effect proof or verified contract change.

naya_view.directive: Maintain operational severity and causal diagnosis as separate fields on every incident. Calibrate L1 statistical gates per endpoint with matched baselines and documented false-alert tolerance; never let a confirmed duplicate wait for a trend. Count logical operations with disclosed unobserved outcomes; stratify by every scope dimension. Require the six-point proof for duplicate-effect claims; treat HTTP statuses as diagnostic inputs. Run the fast safety gate and the slow diagnosis as separate stages; record precaution distinctly from established fact. Withdraw atomically at the consequential-use boundary; requalify narrowly and independently. Apply the same evidence discipline to our own operational attributions.

simple_view.meaning: Timeouts justify investigating, not accusing; one proven double-effect justifies pulling the guarantee immediately. Alert on risk, prove on evidence, and always say which is which.
